subject: 17. “ASN without GDN” must be restricted in the absence of an approved cost sheet.

candidates.text: “ASN without GDN” must be restricted in the absence of an approved cost sheet.
The system only validates the OC details and does not check the cost sheet or stock for the style, since it is a non-GDN ASN.
Mostly this transaction is done where an OC has FOT type “commission” and the fulfillment type is “None”

But during review, we observed that in some cases users need to create an ASN without a GDN even when the FOT type is not “commission” and fulfilment type is not “None.” In such scenarios, the system again only validates the OC details, skips checking cost sheet approval, and the data does not flow to model OPR/OCR.

If an OC has the fulfilment type set to anything other than “None” (e.g., Back Order, Purchase, Manufacture) and the user creates a Sale ASN without GDN, the system must validate both the OC details and the cost sheet.
If the cost sheet has not been approved at least once, the system should display an alert message.
The user should be permitted to proceed only if the cost sheet has been approved at least once.
If the fulfilment type is anything other than “None” (e.g., Back Order, Purchase, Manufacture):
The system must validate both the OC details and the cost sheet.
The user will be allowed to proceed only if the cost sheet has been approved.
The system will not follow the cost sheet validation

Validation:
1. If the fulfilment type is anything other than “None” (e.g., Back Order, Purchase, Manufacture):
2. The system must validate both the OC details and the cost sheet.
3. The user will be allowed to proceed only if the cost sheet has been approved.
4. If the fulfilment type is “None”:
5. The system will not follow the cost sheet validation

chunks.title: 1. Current Functionality
chunks.heading: 1. Current Functionality
chunks.text:
Currently, if a user creates a Sale ASN without GDN. The system only validates the OC details and does not check the cost sheet or stock for the style, since it is a non-GDN ASN. Mostly this transaction is done where an OC has FOT type “commission” and the fulfillment type is “None”
But during review, we observed that in some cases users need to create an ASN without a GDN even when the FOT type is not “commission” and fulfilment type is not “None.” In such scenarios, the system again only validates the OC details, skips checking cost sheet approval, and the data does not flow to model OPR/OCR. This leads to variances appearing in reports
Factory Order Type - CMPT FOC / CMPT LC / Commission / Confirmed / FOB
Fulfilment type - back order / none / manufacturing / purchase

chunks.title: Validation
chunks.heading: Validation
chunks.text:
When creating a Sale ASN without GDN, the system will first check the fulfilment type of the OC.
• If the fulfilment type is anything other than “None” (e.g., Back Order, Purchase, Manufacture):
• The system must validate both the OC details and the cost sheet.
• The user will be allowed to proceed only if the cost sheet has been approved.
• If the fulfilment type is “None”:
• The system will not follow the cost sheet validation
